_README: TWO RULES, AND THEY ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE:
1. THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. Adding an entry is a deliberate decision made by a
human who has understood the defect — never a convenience to make a red build
green. If you are here because the build is failing, the correct move is almost
always to fix the column or the reference, not to add a line to this file.
2. EVERY ENTRY IS A KNOWN DEFECT, NOT AN ACCEPTED STATE. Each line below is a live
bug: Postgres rejects the ENTIRE statement when any named column is unknown, so
each of these breaks a whole query at runtime, not merely one field.
This list exists only so that the alarm could be installed before the 13 pre-existing
defects were fixed. Without it, main could not build today and nothing could ship —
including the schema fixes these entries are themselves waiting on.
Populated 2026-08-01 from the EXPECTED-BUT-ABSENT section of docs/SCHEMA-REFERENCE.md.
The check's independent static extraction reproduced exactly these 13 and no others.
To resolve an entry: either create the column in the Supabase SQL editor and re-export
the snapshot (docs/schema/README.md), or fix/remove the code reference. Then delete the
entry here. The check reports allowlist entries it no longer detects, so stale lines
surface on the next build rather than lingering.
